Patch Set 2:

(14 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. Two of them (the GFP_ATOMIC downgrade in ldebugfs_stats_alloc() and the ls_index handling in the new ldebugfs_stats_register()) are in the lprocfs/nodemap part of the change, which the commit message doesn't describe at all.

The request from the earlier revision to break this up still looks unaddressed: the stats-dump fixes are self-contained bug fixes that could land on their own, the lprocfs_stats_register()/nodemap stats wiring is a third independent piece, and the lustre_obd_nl_* framework still has no in-tree caller (LUSTRE_CMD_HEALTH implements its own start/dump/done rather than using it).

LUSTRE_CMD_HEALTH has no userspace consumer either -- liblustreapi_param.c only handles LUSTRE_CMD_DEVICES and LUSTRE_CMD_STATS -- and no test. Should this add a sanity/conf-sanity case that exercises the new command, so the key table and the unhealthy-device list get covered?

Some concerns, see inline comments.

Splitting is still open from patchset 1: the stats-dump fixes and the new framework are independent, and the stats fixes are the crash-class part that would be easiest to review and backport on their own.

commit.subject: LU-19768 obdclass: table-driven netlink framework
commit.message:
LU-19768 obdclass: table-driven netlink framework

Introduce a reusable table-driven netlink handler framework
(lustre_nl_obd_ops / lustre_nl_ctx) that factors out the common
start/dump/done pattern shared by commands that iterate OBD devices.

Each command supplies a descriptor with collect, dump_one, and
optional release callbacks.

Also fix several bugs in the existing stats dump path:
- Add missing nla_put return-value checks
- Fix an off-by-one in key-list sizing
- Fix a typo ("togther" -> "together").
